As for the laws of the priesthood and the Levitical service, they are known and clear in the Book of God. As for the laws of the House of David: the Book's saying — "O House of David, thus said the Lord: judge justly in the morning, and deliver the despoiled from the hand of the oppressor" (Jeremiah 21:12). Whoever has perfected them, seeking the satisfaction of God, God has singled him out by a blessing in this world and an abundant reward in the next world. He becomes a chosen prophet, or a guided friend [of God], as the Book said concerning Pinhas: "Then Pinhas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; and it was counted to him for righteousness, from generation to generation, forever" (Psalms 106:30–31), and He said: "The priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of My sanctuary when the children of Israel went astray from Me — they shall draw near to Me to serve Me" (Ezekiel 44:15). Whoever of them disobeyed God by it fell from the totality of the high ranks in this world and obtained painful torment in the next world, as you have come to know from the case of Korah and his followers.

**The fourth kind**: God's blessing upon a person among the persons of the people, special to him beyond the rest of his clan and his tribe and the rest of the rational beings — such as a chosen prophet, or a friend [of God] appointed as successor for the management of the nation, or a wise man inspired with knowledge, understanding, and counsel, and the like. For every blessing among these, an additional obedience to God (mighty and exalted) is incumbent upon him.

Whoever has rendered them up — for him is the perpetuity of the totality of the general and particular blessings in this world, and God adds to him strength for it and insight into it — as He said: "The Lord has sworn to David in truth, He will not turn back from it: 'Of the fruit of your body I will set upon your throne; if your sons keep My covenant and My testimony that I will teach them, their sons also forever shall sit upon your throne'" (Psalms 132:11–12). And the abundant reward in the next world, as the Friend said: "If I had not believed to see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living!" (Psalms 27:13).

Whoever has disobeyed God in the blessing with which He singled him out has fallen from the totality of the excellences; the reckoning upon him is the more severe in this world, as He said: "This is what the Lord has spoken, saying: 'I will be sanctified through those near to Me, and before all the people I will be honored'; and Aaron held his peace" (Leviticus 10:3), and He said: "Only you have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities" (Amos 3:2). The punishment upon him in the next world is the more emphatic, as He said: "For Tophet is ordained of old, indeed for the king it is prepared" (Isaiah 30:33).

By these four kinds, obedience to God is incumbent upon the people. For every blessing God adds upon the human, an obedience for it is incumbent. The evidence for this is that the tithes attach to grain-products, as it is said: "You shall tithe diligently all the produce of your seed" (Deuteronomy 14:22). Whoever God has blessed with a hundred *mudd* of food owes from it ten *mudd* to God; whoever God has blessed with ten *mudd* owes to God a single *mudd*. If the first surrenders to God nine-and-a-half *mudd* and the second surrenders to God a single complete *mudd*, the first deserves the punishment and the second the reward.

Likewise the speech concerning one who has not been granted a child: the obligations of his circumcision and teaching him the Book of God fall from him. So too whoever is lame — the obligations of pilgrimage fall from him; whoever is sick — there fall from him among the commands of the Law what he has no capacity for. By this analogy, whoever God has singled out by an added blessing is bound by an added obedience and worship in thanksgiving for it.

That is why the most excellent of the early ones used to fear when a blessing among God's blessings in this world came upon them, and would dread it on two grounds: **first**, fear of falling short in rendering up the obedience for it and thanksgiving for it, so that it might become a burden upon them in the next world, as the Friend said: "I have become small by reason of all the kindnesses and all the truth You have done to Your servant" (Genesis 32:11). **And the second ground:** wariness lest [their blessing] be God's recompense (exalted be He) for their obedience to Him, so that thereby the reward of their works would be diminished at the return, as the early ones explained "[He] requites those who hate Him to His face, to destroy them" — and in this is sufficiency for you.

**The soul says:** I have understood what you have mentioned. I do not find myself able to render up the rights of God for the general blessing toward the rational beings, much less for what He has singled me out from it. Even if there is in me eagerness and zeal for the performance of an obligation for it, what occurs to my imagination first at the time of its execution is the hope of new blessings from Him; likewise in my thanksgiving to God when I thank Him: I thank Him with my expression for the great blessing He has bestowed upon me, but my care and intent in thanksgiving is the calling-forth of the continuity of the blessing and the increase from it — not the renunciation of increase or perpetuity. If I am at the like of this in my obedience and my thanksgiving to God (exalted be He), out of paucity of purification toward the right of His blessing, what road have I to rendering up the rest of my obedience for the particularities of His blessing upon me? Guide me, then, to the minimum that is binding upon me of obedience to God for it, by which I may earn the perpetuity of it.

The intellect says: As for what you have complained of, of the paucity of your purification in your obedience and your thanksgiving to your Lord, and that your expression is the expression of one who gives thanks but your intent in it the intent of one craving, and that within your inward is the increase from the blessing and the desire for its perpetuity — this is for three failings. **The first** is the intensity of your love for yourself and your eagerness to draw the blessings to her; you do not move a foot toward obedience to God or to obedience of anyone other than Him except that your intent is the enjoyment by pleasures. I have set down for you at the beginning of my treatment of you that you should strive with all your effort in the rejection of this blameworthy trait from yourself; by that I hope for the setting-right of you. **The second failing** — your ignorance of the bounty of the Creator (exalted be He) upon you, so that it falls to your imagination that you will not reach His blessing except by craving it from Him. He has already bestowed bounty upon you of what is in your knowledge and of what is not in your knowledge — and you do not consider the desire of the one who first did this for you. Would you not — had you repelled this imagination from yourself — have purified your obedience and your thanksgiving to Him in your inward, and would not what you hope for have become more emphatic and more obligatory for you on account of this?

**The third failing** — your ignorance of yourself and the state of her management. You see her as worthy of the highest of blessings, and never cease being eager for them; whenever something of them reaches you, your ambition aspires to what is beyond, and you do not see the Creator (exalted be He) as worthy of the most emphatic of obediences. So that, if there be obedience from you, you reckon it as a favor from you toward Him — what is your knowledge of your poverty for Him and His freedom-from-need-of-you? If you removed this ignorance from yourself, and looked with the clear eye, and knew that the Creator (exalted be He) who created you is more solicitous for you than yourself, and more knowing of what is right for you of blessings and what is not right, you would be satisfied and content with what comes to you of them; and your thanksgiving to Him for them would grow great in purification, and you would not attach your hope to what would distract you from discriminating what came to you of them and rendering up the right of God for them. What you have not been worthy of, you must inevitably attain to when you have earned it by your obedience — not when you have hoped for it by attaching your ambition.
As for what you have asked concerning the minimum that is incumbent toward God (exalted be He) of obedience by which the perpetuity of His blessing upon the human is earned — there are ten concepts.
**Among them**: that he should not make [the blessing] a cause of disobedience to Him.
**Among them**: that he should mention the blessing of God upon him with his tongue, and multiply for it praise and thanksgiving in his heart and the outward of his expression.
**Among them**: that he should not deny it nor reckon it too little.
**Among them**: that he should not attribute it to other than God if it was at the hand of an intermediary — thanking the intermediaries and being heedless of thanksgiving to God for it.
**Among them**: that he should not boast in it and let it fall to his imagination that he has taken it by his strength and his subtlety, or by his desert of it.
**Among them**: that it should not fall to his imagination that he perpetuates it by his prudence, and that it perishes from him when he is heedless and squanders it.

**Among them**: that he should not despise the one deprived of these blessings, seeing himself as more excellent than him before God — for perhaps it is a trial from God for him, that there may appear what is hidden in him of evil inwardness, by which he may be deceived. So whoever is deprived [of it] may be more excellent before God than he.

**Among them**: that he should purify his inward, his purification toward God, and his humility toward Him; though he has not added to his action upon what was earlier, and has not added to his thanksgiving and praise — let him be, in the state of [the blessing's] perpetuity, as he was. Let him strive in the purification of his inward at the time of his action for God, and let the blessing not be a cause of falling-short in his earlier action or distracting his mind from the increase in purification toward God.

**Among them**: that his eye be always toward one who is below him in the multitude of blessings, not to one who is above him in them. So too it is fitting for him that his eye be always toward one who has more obedience to God (exalted be He) than himself, that he might aspire to climb to his rank — and not turn to one who has less obedience to God than himself, so as to be self-satisfied with his act and grow heedless concerning it.

**Among them**: that he should not be deceived by the length of God's covering over him and His being patient with him, so that he is safe from His displeasure and disobeys Him. For everyone whose report has reached us from the past, and whom we have witnessed in the present, of those upon whom God bestowed blessings of various kinds and who turned from obedience to God to His disobedience — nothing entered upon them but what I have described to you. This is well-known from the books of the prophets of every era. These are the totality of the corrupters of this Third Gate, whose intent we have set out in the explication of the aspects of binding oneself to obedience to God (exalted be He).

Whoever has not been able to increase in obedience to God when His blessing increases, and has been able to bind himself to what I have described to you for the sake of God (exalted be He) — he deserves the perpetuity of the blessing special to him. If [the blessing] is stripped from him, it is for one of two causes: either as a purging of a prior offense in him, or as a compensation in the house of permanence with what is loftier and more sublime and more ample by far.

**The soul says:** You have treated and you have healed; you have admonished, and you have fulfilled; you have come forth with your light, and you have lifted the darkness of ignorance from me. Yet there remains upon me, from the corrupters of obedience to God, one aspect — and if you heal me from its sickness and lift its concern from me, I shall be saved from the worst of diseases, and shall be on the brink of recovery from all my sicknesses.
The intellect says: And what is the aspect whose location within you is what you have described?

**The soul says:** What I have found in the Book of God (mighty and exalted) concerning the matter of compulsion, predestination, judgment, and will — that all these belong to God in everything He has created among mineral, plant, animal, and rational being — as the Book says: "Whatever the Lord pleased, He did, in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and all the deeps" (Psalms 135:6), and He said: "The Lord brings death and brings life, He brings down to Sheol and brings up; the Lord makes poor and makes rich, He humbles and He exalts" (1 Samuel 2:6–7), and He said: "Who has said and it came to pass, when the Lord has not commanded? Out of the mouth of the Most High come not the evils and the good?" (Lamentations 3:37–38), and He said: "Former of light and Creator of darkness, Maker of peace and Creator of evil" (Isaiah 45:7), and He said: "If the Lord does not build the house, in vain do its builders labor in it; if the Lord does not guard the city, in vain does the watchman stay awake. In vain to you who rise up early, who sit up late, eaters of the bread of toils" (Psalms 127:1–2), and many like this — all of which indicate, in the whole, that the human and the rest of the animals are instruments prepared by the Creator (exalted be He) for the adornment of this world; that if He moves them, they move; that their actions take place by His permission, His power, and His decree; that if He stills them, their actions cease — as He said: "When He is quiet, who can condemn?" (Job 34:29), and He said: "You hide Your face — they are dismayed; You take away their breath — they die, and to their dust they return" (Psalms 104:29). The totality of the reports of the early ones in every book point to this concept, with no disagreement in it.

Then I find the contrary of this in the Book of God (exalted be He) — what indicates that the actions that appear from the human are delegated to him, and that he is given a choice in them, and that they come about from him by his will and his choice; that is why reward and punishment for his obedience and his disobedience have become incumbent upon him. That is the Book's saying: "See, I have set before you this day the life and the good, and the death and the evil" (Deuteronomy 30:15), and He said: "And you shall choose life, that you may live" (Deuteronomy 30:19), and He said: "From your own hands has this come about for you" (Malachi 1:9), and He said: "For the work of man He shall recompense him" (Job 34:11), and He said: "The folly of a man perverts his way, and his heart rages against the Lord" (Proverbs 19:3). The totality of what is in our Book of law, discipline, and admonition points to the validity of this matter; and so does what is in it of reward upon obedience and punishment upon disobedience — all this indicating that the actions of the human are delegated to him, and that God is free of his good and his evil, his beautiful deeds and his foul ones. The matter is intricate to me, and the way to reconcile the two matters is exceedingly difficult — is there any cure for the like of this disease, by which God might heal me at your hands?

The intellect says: There is nothing in what you have described of the difficulty in reconciling the two matters as found in the Book of God and the books of the prophets that is greater than what is found by way of reflection in actuality. For we see the actions of the human take place sometimes according to his intent and his choice, and at other times against his intent and his choice — and this indicates their being upon the bridle of the Creator and His reining-in over them; He releases of them what He wills and withholds what He does not will. This is made manifest to you from him even in the motion of his tongue, his hearing, and his seeing. Then I see that reward and punishment run upon him according to his actions and motions in obedience and disobedience to God.

The disagreement of the learned has been long on the aspect of reconciling compulsion and justice. Among them is the one who said that all the human actions run upon the human's choice, and from his power and capacity — God having delegated their matter to him and ruled him over them, and God (blessed and exalted) being free of them; and that this is why reward and punishment have become incumbent upon him. And among them is the one who returned the human actions, and others, to God (exalted be He) and claimed that every motion that comes about in this world from rational and silent comes about by the permission of the Creator (exalted be He), by His power, His judgment, and His reining-in — nothing escapes Him, nothing is neglected of Him by the measure of a hair, neither what is below it nor what is above. But when they were challenged about the running of reward and punishment, they said: the concept of reward and punishment is unknown to us in its form and the courses of its rulings; God (exalted be He) is just, He does not oppress; truthful in His promise and warning, He does not contradict; and our intellects are too weak to apprehend the kernel of His wisdom; His justice is more renowned and His bounty more manifest than that we should impugn Him in His judgment — there is no god save Him.

And among them is the one who saw the firm conviction of the two schools — I mean justice and compulsion — and claimed that the one who plunges into them is not free from error and missteps however he wills. The right thing, they said, is for us to act the act of the one who firmly believed that the actions are delegated to the human and for them he is rewarded and punished, that we may strive in all that benefits us before God (exalted be He) in both houses; and rely on Him with the reliance of one for whom it has been validated that the kingpin of the actions, motions, benefits, and harms is by God's decree, by His permission, and His reining-in; and that to God (exalted be He) belongs the compelling argument over the human, and the human has no argument against God (mighty and exalted). This view is the nearest to safety of all that has gone before, for it is from truth and fairness the acknowledgment of ignorance of the like of this in the wisdom of God (exalted be He) — on account of the weakness of our intellects and the paucity of our discernment. And in our ignorance of it is an aspect among the aspects of benefit, on account of which it is hidden from us. If our being apprised of this secret had been welfare for us, the Creator (exalted be He) would have uncovered it to us.

And the closest analogies for this — what we see of the state of the weak of vision: he does not benefit from the light of the sun until there is set between it and his sight a subtle veil; the stronger the injury in his sight is, the greater his welfare in the more coarse veil; the lighter the injury in his sight, the more subtle the veil is the better for him. And again — we see, in many corporeal crafts, actions such that if the sense of sight had not fallen upon them, and their report had reached us, we would have hastened to disbelieve the one reporting them. Such as the astrolabe: had we not apprehended it by our eyes — and someone had reported to us its form and shape and what is apprehended by it of the motions of the spheres, the places of the stars, the determining of the hours of every time of the year, the knowledge of the distances of the various things — many like this of the unknown matters would not be validly fixed in our thoughts, nor their form established in our imaginations. And likewise that which is nearer to us among the instruments used among the common people, such as the steelyard balance: had our sense of sight not fallen upon it, it would not have been validly fixed in our souls that one weighs the weight of truth by a balance one of whose sides is longer than the other; and again, the wonder that one weight of it weighs many different weights of more and less. And among what is yet more in use among people: the motion of the upper stone of the mill by circling and equilibration, by weak intermediaries that the water moves; and when we throw a small stone in a running current, it does not pause a moment until it reaches the bottom. In the mill the upper [stone] is many times the weight of the stone thrown in [the current], and the strength of the intermediaries that move the mill is far less than the strength of the current. If a reporter had reported this to us without our witnessing it with our own eyes, we would have hastened to disbelieve and to refute his speech. This is because of our ignorance of the secrets of creation and the weakness of our discernment of the roots of the existents and their branches and their natures and their properties.

Whoever is — in the like of what we have described — of ignorance of what is before him, it is no wonder he is ignorant of the courses of predestination and justice in the rulings of the Maker (exalted be He), which are more hidden and higher than what we have described, immeasurably so. Concerning his like the Friend (peace be upon him) says: "O Lord, my heart is not lifted up, nor my eyes lofty" (Psalms 131:1); and he followed this with what congrues with it of surrender to God by his saying: "Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child upon his mother, like the weaned child is my soul" (Psalms 131:2).

**The soul says:** You have caused me to find familiar what I had given up hope of apprehending of the secret of this matter, on account of its subtlety and the fineness of its concept. But uncover for me the secret of my matter, the intent in my standing in this house; and bring close to me the form of compulsion and justice with the utmost of what is possible of brevity. Let me not be in the state of the one ignorant of the way of his rightness, in what has reached me of the kings — namely, that in some of the islands of India is a city whose people have agreed upon the placing-forward of a foreigner among them every year; when the year is complete for him, they cast him out, in the state he was in before his rule. Among those who held rule over them was a man ignorant of their secret in him: he gathered the moneys, built the palaces and erected them, and did not let out anything from their city; then he aspired to draw in everything that was his outside the city — of money and family — to it. When the year was complete for him, the people of the city expelled him empty of all of it; he was prevented from everything he had built and acquired, anciently or recently. At his going out he found nothing of what had been his in the city or outside; he remained regretful and grieving over his striving and his exertion at what he had built, gathered, and lost to another.

Then the people of that city happened to approve of a foreigner who was possessed of inwardness and understanding. When he held rule over them, he singled out a man among them, treated him well, and dealt subtly with him; then he asked him about the secret of the folk and their custom with whoever had held rule over them before him. He uncovered for him their matter, their secret, and their school. When he knew this from them, he occupied himself with nothing of what the first occupied himself with, but rather strove and exerted himself in bringing out every precious item from that city to another city. He made his treasures and important commodities in some other city, and did not find comfort in their honor and reverence for him. He was, the whole length of his sojourn in the city, between sorrow and joy: as for his sorrow, it was on account of the swiftness of his going out from it and his reckoning small what he was able to bring out from it of useful things — had his standing in it been long, he might have increased in this. As for his joy, it was at the swiftness of his going out from the city, that he might settle in the place where he had placed his treasures, and employ them in the aspects of his benefits and the kinds of his pleasures, with prosperity of mind, quiet of soul, and continuity of state. So when his year ran out, his going out from them did not grieve him; rather, he hastened to it with openhandedness of soul and a clear face, thankful for his striving, praising himself for his action — and he reached the most ample blessing, the most complete dignity, and the most perfect honor in continual joy. He was envied in both states, and attained his hope in both houses.

And I fear that my state may be the state of the ignorant one, who was miserable in both houses and lost the two stations. Since God has now bestowed bounty upon me through you, guide me and give me insight into my state, and what I have stood upon of the secret of my matter and the aspects of my welfare.

The intellect says: You have described, in what you have likened, the form of your station in this world; your state in it is the state of the ones I have described among the kings. Your foreignness and the swiftness of your reversal have now been validated for you — so do as the man of inwardness and understanding did, that your state may be like his. If you turn aside from this, there is no benefit for you in my discourse and no profit in my speech to you.
**The soul says:** Were it not for my eagerness for this, I would not have investigated what is hidden from me of my matter.

The intellect says: As for the secret of your matter: the Creator (exalted be He) created you not from a thing — out of the totality of what He created of the spiritual substances. He wished to ennoble you and raise your rank to the ranks of His chosen ones and the pure of His drawn-near to His light — as bounty upon you and beneficence to you. You were not worthy of this except after three things: **the first**, the uncovering of the veil of ignorance from you and your being illumined by knowing Him; **the second**, your trial and testing by your own choice — for His obedience or for His disobedience; **the third**, your disciplining in this house and your patience over the burden of His servitude in it, that He might raise you to the rank of the lofty ones and the patient, of whom the Friend said: "Bless the Lord, His angels, mighty in strength, doers of His word, hearkening to the voice of His word" (Psalms 103:20). This was not possible in you while you were in your first state.

So it was from the wisdom of the Creator (exalted be He) that He created for you this world, with everything it contains of mineral, plant, and animal, by the most firmly-knit order and the soundest management — made ready for your welfares. Then He extracted for you, from the pure of its elements, a firmly-built temple, resembling the world in its roots, its branches, and its form. Then He opened in it for you five gates to the [outer] world, and arranged in them five gatekeepers of His trusted ones — as for the gates, they are the instruments of the senses, which are the two eyes, the two ears, the nose, the tongue, and the two hands; as for the gatekeepers, they are the five senses employed in them, namely the sense of sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch — by which you reach all your welfares in this world.

Then He prepared for you, inside that temple, four quarters for the four officers that manage it: the brain, the heart, the liver, and the testes. Then He arranged inside it also four storehouses for four stewards — I mean the attractive power, the retentive power, the digestive power, and the expulsive power; their storehouses and dwellings are the two biles, the black bile and the yellow bile, the phlegm and the blood, for the welfares of the temple. Then He distributed the household inside it and outside it for its preservation and protection: as for those inside, such as the entrails, the vessels, the muscles, the nerves, and the arteries; as for those outside, the two hands, the two feet, the tongue, the genitals, the nails, the teeth, and the like. Then He prepared for you in it bindings and intermediaries between the spiritual and the corporeal — namely the blood, the innate heat, and the animal spirit.

Then He bound you to this temple by a firmly-knit binding and an arranged tether by His power (exalted be He) and His wisdom, that the three things that I have mentioned to you might be perfected for you in it. Then He arranged for you, in your inner court, two viziers, and set over you two scribes, and gave you of the retainers and the agents in your presence according to your need in this house. As for the two viziers, one of them is the intellect, who guides you to what is the satisfaction of God with you; as for the second vizier, it is your passion, which leads you astray and carries you to what displeases God your Creator. As for the two scribes, one of them is the scribe of your good deeds — what comes from you in secret and openly, inward and outward, by the hands of the agents employed in them, from all the previously mentioned gatekeepers, officers, agents, retainers, viziers, slaves, and acting-men; the second scribe is the scribe of the bad deeds, on the model of what was mentioned with the good deeds. As for the slaves and the acting-men, they are the traits of the soul — such as joy, care, gladness, sorrow, remembrance, forgetting, knowledge, ignorance, courage, cowardice, oppression, justice, shame, audacity, hope, despair, love, hatred, pleasure, pain, vainglory, humility, sovereignty, abasement — and many like these that you employ in the inward of your matter.

Then the Creator (exalted be He) covenanted with the gatekeepers, officers, agents, retainers, viziers, slaves, and acting-men to be led by you and halt at your command for a fixed term, except in particular matters that He has explained to them at the time of their binding-to-you — and this is the concept of compulsion and the place of predestination.

Then He released to you the deployment of all of them in the welfares of your body, and in all that has been delegated to you to use in this world — in known aspects and particular matters, namely the totality of the rational laws, the heard laws, and the permitted. And He said to you: All that I have committed to you and delegated its deployment to you in this world — do not be deceived by it; for it does not add a thing to your essence, nor does it diminish it; no pleasure or pain reaches you from it. They are only things passing upon your body from inside or outside it; nothing of it is special to you. Its placement in you is the placement of the afterbirth from the newborn, the placement of the shell of the egg from the chick. If you have discriminated from Me and understood My intent in you and My blessing upon you, and have chosen My obedience and ceased from My disobedience in the management of all I have committed to you — I command your being joined to the loftiest degree of My pure ones and My chosen ones; I bring you near to My mercy and clothe you with the light of My honor. If you have preferred My disobedience, I shall punish you with the most severe of punishments and the longest of torments. If you are ignorant of the aspects of deploying their matter in any of the things I have bound you to the upholding of in My obedience — on account of your preoccupation with your body and its tribulations by which I have tried you — I have singled you out by a wise, counseling vizier: if you consult him, he will guide you; if you grow heedless, he will awaken you. He is the intellect. Consult him in all your matters; he will command you to deploy all who are with you in the aspects of My obedience, so that your blameworthy traits return as praiseworthy — as the skilled physician does, who deploys the medicines whose ordinary action is harmful, for the benefit of bodies, like poisons and the like.

If you are upon this school — in preferring your intellect and taking up his view — the scribe of the good deeds writes the whole of your permitted motions in the totality of your good deeds, and they will be an addition to them, and every one who acts for you will be an aid to My obedience. But if you contradict his view and incline to the view of the second vizier — opposed to him in all his states — and deploy all of them in what he points you to, your praiseworthy traits return as blameworthy, like the ignorant physician who kills with beneficial medicines on account of his ignorance of the aspects of taking them. And the scribe of the bad deeds writes the whole of your permitted motions in the totality of your bad deeds, and they will be an addition upon them. You will find your helpers, your agents, your slaves, and all you have to do with conforming to you and to your choice — so you will increase in envy and joy. But all this is justice from your Creator on account of your preferring His disobedience over His obedience — or His obedience over His disobedience — in your inward and your intent in the inner of your matter; for the outer and the inner of you are equal before Him. He requites you according to what He sees of this — even if it is hidden from people. Do you not see that the judge rules according to what is validly established in his sight by witnesses or by his senses; and if what is in the inwards were validly established in his sight, he would rule by it? The Creator (exalted be He) whose knowledge of the whole of this is equal — it is incumbent that He rule by what He knows. That is as the Book said: "The hidden things belong to the Lord our God" (Deuteronomy 29:28).

When God wishes to awaken you and chasten you, He commands one of those acting for you to turn his care from you, so that limb of your body grows ill, or two limbs, or all of it; he is sick and weakens for a known stretch of time. If you wake up and return to him, He commands him to turn his care back to you; your body is healed and returns to its first state — as the Book said: "Fools, because of the way of their transgression and because of their iniquities, are afflicted; their soul abhors all food, and they draw near to the gates of death; then they cry to the Lord in their distress, and He saves them from their afflictions; He sends out His word and heals them, and rescues them from their corruptions" (Psalms 107:17–20).

When the term of your trial in this world has passed, the Creator (exalted be He) commands the whole of the agents, the acting-men, the gatekeepers, the household, and the slaves whom we have mentioned to depart from you. The bindings and intermediaries that are between you and your body unwind; you return to your first state. Your body remains with no motion and no sensation, and it also returns to its first state, as the Wise One said: "The dust shall return to the earth as it was, and the spirit shall return to God who gave it" (Ecclesiastes 12:7).

The pages of your acts and your thoughts and your choice and what you preferred and busied yourself with in your this-world are presented before you; the requital falls accordingly from the Creator (exalted be He) toward you. He has emphatically confirmed this for you, and warned and again warned by the hand of His messengers, His prophets, and His truthful Book, as the Friend (peace be upon him) said: "Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to my knowledge; for it is pleasant if you keep them in your inward parts, that they may be ready together upon your lips. So that your trust may be in the Lord, I have made known to you this day, even you. Have I not written to you excellent things in counsels and knowledge, to make you know the certainty of the words of truth, that you might bring back words of truth to those who send you?" (Proverbs 22:17–21).

**The soul says:** I have understood your discourse and remembered the whole of what you have mentioned. Now I am pleading at the noble of your good qualities — that you make clear for me the proper deployments of the praiseworthy and blameworthy among my traits, which, if I deploy in their proper places, I shall be praised for, and thanked for my employing them in them.

The intellect says: Your traits are many — but I shall mention what is at hand to me, in brief. **In your traits are two traits**: joy and sorrow — and they are contraries. The proper deployment of joy: when you are at home with an enduring, perpetual pleasure that is not muddied by spoiling and that no injury overtakes — let loose this trait. As for the place of the deployment of sorrow: when an enduring, perpetual distressing matter comes to you in which you have no contrivance for warding off and no aspect for parting with — let loose the trait of sorrow at that, and employ it.

**Among your traits are two traits**: fear and hope. The place of fear is when your state leads to a state that disquiets you, whose outcome does not conform to you, and you have no power or capacity to repel it from yourself. The place of hope is in striving in the antecedents that bring about beneficence to you and the bestowing of blessings upon you, when no preventer prevents this and no cause interposes against it — such as conforming to what God (exalted be He) has commanded to be done, for its beautiful outcome.

**Among your traits are two traits**: courage and cowardice. The place of the deployment of courage is in setting forth to kill the enemies of God, and patience to bear every labor and every trial in the satisfaction of God (exalted be He) and in the satisfaction of His friends, as He said: "For Your sake we are killed all the day; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter" (Psalms 44:23), and He said: "Let the righteous strike me — it is kindness; let him reprove me" (Psalms 141:5). As for the place of cowardice: in setting forth to kill the friends of God and the possessors of obedience to Him, and in holding back from confronting those who exhort you with what is your welfare, as He said: "Because your heart was soft, and you were humbled before the Lord" (2 Kings 22:19).

**Among your traits are two traits**: shame and audacity. The place of shame: at the disobedience of the One who has bestowed blessing upon you, in His presence and before His face; at His reproach of you with His promise and His threat; and at the meeting of His messengers, as He said: "Son of man, declare to the children of Israel the matter of the House [of God], and they shall be ashamed of their iniquities" (Ezekiel 43:10), and He said: "My God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to You, my God" (Ezra 9:6). As for the place of the trait of audacity: at the meeting of the transgressor, the people of disobedience, and the masters of discourse among the opponents of the truth; and in commanding the recognized good and forbidding the rejected; at rebuking the disobedient, the chiding of the common people and the elite, as He said: "I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame" (Isaiah 50:7); and He said: "Like adamant, harder than flint, I have made your forehead" (Ezekiel 3:9); and He said: "And I shall speak of Your testimonies before kings, and shall not be ashamed" (Psalms 119:46).

So too the two traits of contentment and anger. The place of anger: at lack of fairness, going outside the rule of justice, and the preferring of falsehood and its people over the possessors of truth. The place of contentment: at placing things in their proper places and ranking them in their proper ranks, and running upon the path of truth in them.

So too the two traits of mercy and severity. The place of mercy: with the people of want, weakness, and sickness; with those who renounce the world; with the weak of discrimination concerning the aspects of his welfare; with the ignorant in the management of his soul; with the captive in the hand of his enemy; with the one deprived of an earlier blessing; with the one regretful of his disobedience to his Lord; with the one weeping over the offenses that have passed for him out of fear of God's punishment. As for the place of severity: in taking God's rights from the disobedient, and in vengeance upon the corrupters in the earth, as the Book says: "Your eye shall not pity him" (Deuteronomy 13:9), and He said: "You shall not have mercy and shall not cover him" (Deuteronomy 13:9).

So too the two traits of pride and humility. The place of pride and disdain: when there come to you the people of ignorance of God and those turned away from Him — do not be humble or submissive to them in such a way that there appears from you confirmation of them and influence-by their corrupt schools; rather, let loose the trait of disdain and pride that indicates the contrary of their view and the paucity of contentment with them — as you know from the story of Mordecai and Haman. The place of the deployment of humility: at your meeting one of bounty, righteousness, and pure-belief in God, knowledgeable of His Book, acting by obedience to Him, or one who has on you a blessing and beneficence binding you to its requital — and how much more for the One whose blessing has been too majestic and too great for you to requite Him for it; and likewise at God's taking justice from you, as He said: "Then their uncircumcised heart will be humbled, and then they shall make amends for their iniquity" (Leviticus 26:41).

So too the two traits of love and hatred. The place of love: let it be for the one who conforms to you in obedience to God, and in what gladdens you in the outcome of your matter. The place of hatred: for whoever opposes the satisfaction of God and contends with the people of truth, and leads you to what displeases your Lord against you, as He said: "Those who forsake the Law praise the wicked, but those who keep the Law contend with them" (Proverbs 28:4).

So too the two traits of generosity and stinginess. The place of generosity: the placing of every thing in its place, and giving every possessor of excellence of knowledge and wealth according to what he is worthy of, as the Friend (peace be upon him) said: "Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due when it is in the power of your hand to do it" (Proverbs 3:27); and he said: "Your fountains shall be dispersed abroad" (Proverbs 5:16). As for the place of stinginess: with the people of severity, dullness, and ignorance of their own worth and the worth of the blessing upon them, as He said: "He who reproves a scoffer takes shame for himself, and he who reproves a wicked man — his blemish" (Proverbs 9:7), and our early ones (peace be upon them) said: "Whoever does good to one who does not recognize him is as if he cast a stone at Mercurius" (b. Hullin 133a).

So too the two traits of indolence and zeal. The place of the deployment of indolence: in the brutish appetites whose pleasure passes from the human and there remains upon him in this world its disgrace and in the next world its punishment. As for the place of zeal: in the spiritual pleasures and the actions by which the satisfaction of God (exalted be He) is sought, as the Friend (peace be upon him) said: "I made haste, and did not delay to observe Your commandments" (Psalms 119:60).

In what I have mentioned in this gate is sufficiency for whoever seeks guidance and asks for the truth for its own sake, and seeks knowledge for its essence. May God grant us and you success in what is His obedience, by His mercy.
